svg.title: Thermal programming of phase assemblage, dissolution, interfacial pH and cytocompatibility in Ca–Si–P–O glass-ceramics (700 vs 1100 °C)
svg.desc: Four panels. A: phase composition and bulk density versus sintering temperature. B: mass loss versus immersion time with Korsmeyer–Peppas fits. C: interfacial pH versus time. D: cell viability versus extract concentration.
svg.text: Thermal programming of phase architecture and ion release
700 °C peaks at pH 8.55 (3 d); 1100 °C stays in window
Shaded: pH 7.35–7.85 physiological window · Dashed: pH 8.2
Table 1 | Ion release after 21 d immersion
Release is ≈ 4× higher at 700 °C; the Ca : Si ratio is unchanged at both temperatures.
Figure 1 | Sintering temperature programs phase assemblage, dissolution, interfacial pH and cytocompatibility of Ca–Si–P–O glass-ceramics. (A) Phase
fractions (stacked bars, wt%) and bulk density (dashed line, right axis) after sintering at 700–1100 °C. (B) Cumulative mass loss during immersion;
symbols are measured values and lines are Korsmeyer–Peppas fits (M = k·tⁿ). (C) Interfacial pH over 21 d; the shaded band marks the physiological
window (pH 7.35–7.85) and the dashed line marks pH 8.2. (D) Cell viability versus extract concentration relative to untreated control; the dashed line
is the 70% cytotoxicity threshold (ISO 10993-5). Red circles, 700 °C; blue squares, 1100 °C.
